instruments.title: School Gender Identity Policies (enacts Utah Code 53E-9-205, 'Parental right to student information')
instruments.operative_summary: A school or LEA may not adopt a policy or action that shields a student's education record from the parent, or that interferes with the parent's access to information about the child. A school may not stop a parent from accessing the child's education record. A school may not change a student's education record on gender identity (where it does not conform to sex) without written parental consent. The bill does NOT write a notice duty for staff and does not mention names or pronouns in speech. The safety exception is cross-referenced to 53E-9-203(6).
instruments.operative_quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a school or LEA may not: (a) prohibit a parent of a child from accessing the child's education record; or (b) without written parental consent make changes to a student's education record regarding a student's gender identity that does not conform with the student's sex.
instruments.rung_note: Main act = parents get access on request, and no policy may shield the record from them (rung 3). Subsection (3)(b) adds written parental consent before a gender-identity change to the RECORD. That is close to rung 5, but it covers records, not staff use of names/pronouns. The coder must decide whether (3)(b) reaches rung 5. Note: USBE guidance and Provo policy read (3)(b) as requiring parent permission for a different name/pronoun, but the statute text does not say 'name' or 'pronoun'. Statute unchanged since 2023 (code page shows one version only).

instruments.title: Public Employee Gender-specific Language Requirements
instruments.operative_summary: 1st substitute (the text that passed the House) amends 53G-10-206. It bars the State Board or an LEA from disciplining school staff solely because the staff member called a student by a name/pronoun that (i) matches birth name or sex, used in good faith without knowing a preference; (ii) the student prefers, or, where the parent states a preference, the name the parent prefers; or (iii) fits the employee's religious or moral beliefs. It does not require anyone to tell parents, and does not require parent permission before staff use a name.
instruments.operative_quote: (c) pursue disciplinary action against an individual who is instructional personnel or administrative personnel solely because the individual, in relation to a student, referred to the student by a name, pronoun, or other gender-specific language: ... (ii)(A) except as provided in Subsection (3)(c)(ii)(B), that the student prefers; or (B) that the student's parent prefers;
instruments.rung_note: Fits no rung. It is a discipline shield for staff speech. It ranks the parent's name preference above the student's for the shield, but it states no act on telling parents or on parental permission. Listed so the coder can see it was checked.

school_board_policies.id: Provo City SD Policy 3300 'Gender Inclusive Schools' (update approved 2025-09-09 per file name)
school_board_policies.operative_quote: The unofficial records of the student shall reflect the preferred name and gender identity of the student, but only if requested by the parent. ... Unofficial records which reflect a student's sex, gender, or gender identity may not be changed to a gender or gender identity which does not conform with the student's sex without written permission of the student's parent.
school_board_policies.second_quote: A student's transgender status shall not be disclosed to individuals other than the student's parent without the student's and parent's consent.
school_board_policies.rung_note: Preferred name goes on school records only if the PARENT requests it; written parent permission before any record change. That is consent-first (rung 5) for records, and it reaches unofficial records (class lists etc.), which is wider than the state law. The 'not disclosed to anyone other than the parent' line confirms parents are not the ones kept out.
school_board_policies.implements_mandate: PARTLY. The official-record consent sentence copies 53E-9-205(3)(b). The 'only if requested by the parent' rule for UNOFFICIAL records goes beyond state text. Flag for the coder.

school_board_policies.id: Provo City SD Policy 3228 P1 'Preferred Student Name and/or Gender Identity Change Request Procedures' (last modified 2023-12-01)
school_board_policies.operative_quote: For purposes of this procedure, an Authorized Party is: a parent or legal guardian of an unemancipated student 17 years old or younger; a student 18 years of age or older; or an emancipated student of any age
school_board_policies.rung_note: For a minor, only the parent may request the preferred name/pronouns/gender change. This is an administrative PROCEDURE (P1), not a board-voted policy; no board vote found. Implements 53E-9-205 in part.
